html:
SMTO-EXE-0269 — This workflow is waiting for you to answer a question

GUID: a7925b62-ce1a-56c4-8caa-a7fec34be5a9
Slug: recipe-manual-interaction-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • One step in this workflow needs a person to confirm or answer something. The workflow is paused at that step and won't go on until you answer. SMTO never answers it for you.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Go to the conversation where this workflow is running. If a schedule started it, open Schedules, find it and select Open run. The run's conversation shows the exact question this step is waiting on.
  2. Read SMTO's question in that conversation, type your answer in the message box and send it. The paused step only finishes after you answer that specific question.
  3. If the run shows no question waiting for you, don't start the workflow again yet. First check in the run which steps already finished. Starting it again could repeat a step that already changed something, such as sending a message twice.

What success looks like

  • The run no longer shows Waiting for input, and the workflow moves on to its next step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start a new run of the workflow while the earlier run is still unfinished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A recorded workflow reached a manual or confirmation step that must be answered through the normal Ask User wait before later steps can run (retained kind; current code tracks this as step status waiting_user rather than emitting this error).

What this means

  • This retained error kind describes a manual workflow checkpoint, but current checkpoint handling records waiting_user through the ordinary Ask User path without directly emitting this kind. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • This retained error kind describes a manual workflow checkpoint, but current checkpoint handling records waiting_user through the ordinary Ask User path without directly emitting this kind.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current pending Ask User checkpoint and its operation identity; the retained label alone does not prove a new checkpoint exists.

How to fix it

  • Answer the pending Ask User wait in the run's conversation; recipes.runtime.checkpoint_answered marks the matching waiting_user step completed only after the human-input path accepts the reply. If no wait is pending, inspect the run's step_states in the recipe run history instead of forcing the step, and never repeat a write step whose outcome is unknown.
  • Answer the actual pending Ask User checkpoint; if none exists, inspect the workflow state instead of inventing approval.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing human-input boundary accepts an answer and the matching manual step completes.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
